frameworks.change: Preserve the existing framework reach and the Windows-only net472 condition. The front door and Workflows use the full framework set. net8.0 retirement belongs to a later release.

applied.authority: Approved framework decision in c526a10ad2; no framework is dropped in 3.6.

notes: OfficeIMO.Pdf grants InternalsVisibleTo to OfficeIMO.Word and OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf (and 20 others): PdfImageExportEngine is internal and Word/PowerPoint image export depends on it.
PDF also exposes 27 PdfOperationResult<PdfDocument> *Result operations; the throwing/Result merge rule needs a decision for operations, not only conversions.
openQuestions: PdfReadDocument/PdfDocumentReadResult internalization requires moving the reading API (pages, text, forms, outlines, structured extraction) onto PdfDocument - the largest single PDF change.
27 PdfOperationResult<PdfDocument> *Result operations: apply the throwing/Result merge rule to operations too?
Create(Action<PdfDocumentBuilder>) is a compose-callback API; confirm it is the PDF object model rather than a second authoring style.

Dropping the Windows-only net472 TFM means .NET Framework consumers run the netstandard2.0 build. #if NETFRAMEWORK workarounds (Word Save snapshot, Excel non-seekable stream save, PDF NET472 branches) must become runtime checks, and the netstandard2.0 build must be tested on .NET Framework 4.7.2 (PSWriteOffice on Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the main consumer).

extraChanges.subject: PdfDocument native output policy
extraChanges.note: PdfSaveOptions.AllowLoss guards private serialization before file/stream publication. A per-output AsyncLocal diagnostic scope captures nested page options and avoids persistent deduplication bypass on repeated saves.

extraChanges.subject: PdfDocument read ownership
extraChanges.note: PdfDocumentReader and PdfInspector were already internal in the starting branch; existing PdfDocument.Read/Inspect and capability properties remain the canonical advanced reading API. PdfReadDocument is parser plumbing.

extraChanges.subject: Pdf read options merge
extraChanges.note: Parsing and semantic extraction options share PdfLoadOptions; defensive clones retain selection, profile and pipeline settings. Pages supports IReadOnlyList<PdfReadPage> without exposing PdfReadDocument.

extraChanges.subject: Reconstruction option capture
extraChanges.note: PDF-to-Word clones retain FailOnLoss; PDF-to-PowerPoint captures parsing options and font faces independently for front-door execution.

extraChanges.subject: Read-only inspection and preservation types use Info
extraChanges.note: Phase A naming follows the approved rule that read-only snapshots end in Info. Geometry properties remain unchanged for Phase B.

extraChanges.subject: Standard-font kerning under modern trimming analysis
extraChanges.note: Expanded the null-coalescing array-element assignment into explicit allocation and assignment. The SDK 10.0.113 ILLink analyzer threw AD0001 in GetStandardFontKerning for the combined expression; kerning behavior and enabled analyzers are preserved.

extraChanges.subject: Completed conversion ownership and consumer grammar
extraChanges.note: ToPdf renders and reopens a private artifact before returning its shared report, so writer-time findings, page counts and FailOnLoss are complete. It returns the original authoring model so callers can continue editing; subsequent native saves retain the normal AllowLoss policy.

extraChanges.change: Native Save preserves the existing chunked serializer, caller-owned stream overwrite/rewind, cancellation and exact-artifact commit semantics. Strict generated stream saves stage in a private file so writer-time loss is rejected before destination writes without buffering the complete artifact in memory.
extraChanges.reason: Focused source-passthrough tests found whole-buffer copies lost mid-write cancellation after the lifecycle consolidation.

extraChanges.note: Merge uses documents first, one optional PdfMergeOptions bag and optional cancellation. The out PdfMergeReport overload retains the policy and readback evidence formerly returned by MergeResult.

The bounded RawStructure reading capability is exposed on PdfDocument. Studio workspace publication retains private save evidence through InternalsVisibleTo so its optimistic source-change guards continue to use the hash of the exact written artifact after native Save becomes void.

Ordered encoded images and image-path collections expose ToPdf/out-report/ToPdfAsync and shared-report SaveAsPdf forms. PdfImageImportOptions.FailOnLoss is snapshotted, render findings use the native diagnostic scope, and generated models are disposed on failed conversion or after saving. Internal image-page construction remains available to OCR, scan composition and printing without a redundant serialization step.

Specialized static content-safety, provenance and signature inspection entry points are internal native kernels. OfficeDocument.Inspect(path, OfficeInspectOptions) returns OfficeDocumentInfo with selectable typed reports and optional native content. IncludeContent=false preserves inspection without content extraction; original package/signature/provenance guards and explicit provider selection remain in their owning libraries. Provenance takes an independent options snapshot with caller cancellation.

Strict adapter PDF saves use the existing staged writer with shared report acceptance before publication. Source-stage and writer-time losses throw OfficeConversionException carrying OfficeConversionReport; native advanced result policies keep their existing behavior. The same writer and file/stream publication owners are reused. Front-door HTML/TXT saves dispose the generated model.

PdfProjectionOptions gains snapshotted FailOnLoss for normalized Reader source conversions. Image collection saves use shared strict report acceptance at the same private staged writer as all Tier 1 PDF adapters.

Native PDF fixture serialization accepts loss explicitly where the fixture intentionally exercises approximation, clipping or unsupported text. Dedicated default-rejection and destination-protection contracts remain strict. Removed two reflection-only tests that required the deleted ToPdfDocument/Result/Bytes and SaveAsPdfResult families.

Native output scopes also capture explicitly supplied PdfConversionReport findings; callers retain their report and writer-time strict checks see the same findings. Measurement-only font views suppress diagnostics so they cannot consume render diagnostic deduplication entries.

Consumer tests use shared conversion reports, explicit loss acceptance for intentionally clipped fixtures and cancellation assertions that accept derived canceled-task exceptions. Removed reflection assertions that only pinned deleted conversion twins; retained actual read limits, page selection and source-options isolation proof.

The native writer paint diagnostic families now select the 25 M1 catalog constants directly. Prefix/suffix composition no longer emits the retired PascalCase identities; occurrence locations, clipping classification and unassessed bounds behavior are preserved.
Existing PowerShell reconstruction tests consume OfficeConversionReport and validate written pages and reconstructed content rather than the removed adapter-specific report types.

Canonical adapter saves wrap serialization failures in OfficeConversionException with the source and PDF output findings. Strict staged saves retain the same failure evidence and preserve caller destinations.
Output-budget failures remain identifiable through nested shared conversion exceptions.
Lossless final file and stream writes preserve completed conversion evidence when publication fails.

Canonical PDF export validates destination arguments before conversion. Later serialization and publication failures retain completed evidence; malformed destination arguments keep their ordinary argument exceptions.

Normal Reader, image and RTF PDF save paths now use the same guarded final-output owner as strict saves. Completed source diagnostics survive file/stream failures; destination arguments are validated before conversion.

InternalsVisibleTo grants the existing browser engine and its tests access to detailed conversion and serialization evidence. This preserves browser diagnostics while keeping conversion kernels outside the public API.

Ten name-based units entries describe raster bytes, aggregate pixel budgets/counters or coordinate density; those APIs remain scalar. Migration generation supports the explicit C# keep action. Physical page and tolerance geometry entries remain pending.
